active_themes.label: Warsh's Credibility Trap
active_themes.summary: Warsh's first Fed meeting arrives this week as the Iran deal creates political cover for easier policy. This is his trap. With 4.2% inflation, 0% spending growth, and markets expecting cuts, Warsh will face immediate pressure to cut or re-confirm his own credibility disaster by signaling rate hikes remain on the table. Public silence = market assumption of cuts into stagflation.

active_themes.label: Iran De-escalation Window
active_themes.summary: Trump announced a deal framework today, collapsing oil to three-month lows and creating genuine 3-7 day relief rally. This is real but temporary: without a formal nuclear agreement and sanctions relief pathway, the window closes as fast as it opened. The market's error is treating oil relief as inflation relief—energy is no longer the binding constraint on the Fed, spending is.

active_themes.label: Lender Silence Continues
active_themes.summary: Discover, Capital One, and Amex had maximum cover today (stagflationary backdrop, flat spending, policy error from Warsh) to announce deposit rate cuts or credit tightening. All three remained silent. This silence will break within 3-7 days as credit market stress forces lenders to move. When it does, it cascades: equities reprice into margin compression and demand destruction.

active_themes.label: Soft Landing Dead
active_themes.summary: May's 0% spending growth + 4.2% inflation + stagnant wages + today's rally confirm equities have not repriced into stagflation. The repricing trigger is lender action (credit tightening or deposit rate cuts), not geopolitical relief. Today's Iran news is a 1-week distraction.

active_themes.label: Yields Stuck at Stagflation Range
active_themes.summary: 10-year remains 3.9-4.1%; 30-year at 2007 highs. Hammack's warning and today's spending data validate stagflation scenario. Yields will not move lower without hard demand destruction (not evident) or inflation rollover (not happening). This is the correct price for an economy cutting rates while inflation stays elevated.

active_themes.label: Bond Market Correct on Yields
active_themes.summary: Yields held firm today (10-year stays at 3.9-4.1%, 30-year near 2007 highs) despite oil collapse and equity rally. Bonds are correctly pricing stagflation—the scenario where the Fed cuts into persistent inflation and demand destruction follows. Today's equity rally into bond flatness confirms the bond market is right and equities are wrong about the path ahead.

active_themes.label: Institutional Silence at Inflection
active_themes.summary: Today's geopolitical relief gave all three major lenders (Discover, Capital One, Amex) cover to delay announcing deposit rate cuts or credit tightening. The silence holds for now. But Iran euphoria fades in 3-7 days, spending remains flat, and lenders will face margin pressure they cannot ignore. This silence breaks under credit stress, not headline relief.

active_themes.label: Soft Landing Dead
active_themes.summary: Today's rally proves equities have not repriced into stagflation—they rallied on a temporary oil relief story instead of repricing into demand destruction. This is the last repricing window before lenders force the issue. May's 0% spending growth + 4.2% inflation + today's rally + Warsh's policy error = equities are wrong, and will correct when credit tightens, not when oil rises again.

open_watchlist.condition: Major lender (Discover, Capital One, Amex) publicly announces deposit rate cuts or tightens consumer credit standards
open_watchlist.meaning: This is the cascade trigger: the market will read it as confirmation that demand is rolling over and the Fed is wrong to cut, forcing a 3-5% equity repricing downward.

open_watchlist.condition: Capital One, Discover, or American Express publicly announces deposit rate cuts or tightens consumer credit standards
open_watchlist.meaning: The institutional repricing cascade begins—equities compress 8-15% as demand destruction becomes visible and margin compression accelerates.

open_watchlist.condition: Warsh or another Fed official publicly states that rate hikes remain on the table through 2027 or beyond
open_watchlist.meaning: The soft-landing delusion dies; equities reprice lower on confirmation that the Fed will not cut into 4.2% inflation, but the repricing is slower and less violent than lender-driven repricing.

open_watchlist.condition: 10-year Treasury yield breaks above 4.1% or 30-year stays at/exceeds 2007 highs for more than 3 consecutive trading days
open_watchlist.meaning: Stagflation expectations are hardening; equities will compress into margin compression and demand destruction risks, regardless of geopolitical relief.

open_watchlist.condition: Capital One, Discover, or American Express announces deposit rate cuts and/or tightens consumer credit standards
open_watchlist.meaning: Lender paralysis has broken and equities will reprice 8-15% lower into demand destruction and margin compression within one week.

open_watchlist.condition: 10-year Treasury yield breaks above 4.1% and stays there for 3+ consecutive trading days
open_watchlist.meaning: Bond market is rejecting the de-escalation relief narrative and repricing stagflation risk; equities follow with 5-8% selloff as multiple compression accelerates.

open_watchlist.condition: Capital One, Discover, or American Express announces deposit rate cuts or tightens consumer credit standards
open_watchlist.meaning: This is the repricing trigger. When lenders move, equities will recognize that the Fed is cutting into stagflation, not into a recoverable economy.

open_watchlist.condition: Warsh or another Fed official publicly states that rate hikes remain on the table through 2027
open_watchlist.meaning: This would break Warsh's credibility trap and signal the Fed sees inflation persistence. It would validate bond yields at 3.9-4.1% and invalidate the market's soft-landing assumption.

open_watchlist.condition: US and Iran announce a formal nuclear deal and concrete sanctions relief timeline beyond June 22
open_watchlist.meaning: This would extend the de-escalation window from 3-7 days to several weeks, delaying the repricing trigger until oil stabilizes and lenders face clearer pressure.

open_watchlist.condition: May and June spending data both confirm 0-1% growth with inflation staying at 4%+
open_watchlist.meaning: This closes off any remaining soft-landing narrative and validates that the repricing is not a matter of if, but when and how deep. Lender action becomes unavoidable.
